# 2022 Marketing Award Honorees

## 2022 Honorees

The National Marketing Awards honors councils who have demonstrated marketing
excellence in building and promoting the Scouting brand through: Fundraising,
Membership Recruitment, Program Implementation, or Social/Digital Outreach. We
celebrate the work of this year’s award-winning councils!

Social / Digital Outreach

###  Atlanta Area Council - Campfire Stories

Great local stories…told on multiple channels…sourced from a team.  The use of
multiple content creators (a.k.a. District Professionals from across the
council) make this effort notable.  No need to rely on one particular person
with the task of mining good content when a lighter load can be spread across
a larger team.  Use all of the resources at your disposal to come up with
great content, and then utilize that content across multiple channels to
maximize your audience reach.  Add in a great hook like “Campfire Stories” and
you have an award-winning combination.  Well done Atlanta Area Council!

[![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_5_-e1663005536369.jpg)](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_5_-e1663005536369.jpg)

Fundraising

###  Piedmont Council - Annual Report

Most annual reports are sent to potential funders, presented to boards, and
included as part of grant proposals. This report was distributed through local
news media in an effort to communicate the impact of Scouting in the
community. In addition, the report has a very simple and clean design that is
consistent with the Piedmont Council’s website.

[![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured7.png)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%20291%20262%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured7.png)

Fundraising

###  Chattahoochee Council - Text to Give

COVID interrupted in-person unit meetings – as well as Friends of Scouting
presentations. In response, the Chattahoochee Council shifted from in-person
“asks” to a digital platform.  They developed a video and adopted a text-to-
give campaign model.  Each unit was assigned a text-to-give code, donations
could be tracked, and units could receive credit for donations. Additionally,
the council created a user-friendly website for families and volunteers to
give. “Most of our families are Millennials who are more comfortable with a
text-to-give platform than a pledge/payment process.  In 2022 we are
replicating the text-to-give campaign, but are changing how we market it to
our units/families,” said Scout Executive Juan Osorio.

Fundraising

###  Dan Beard Council - Merit Badge Sponsorship

Local sponsorships of merit badge programs is an innovative way to involve the
community in the Scouting program, while also providing important financial
support.  A program like this also provides donors a tangible sponsorship
element to embrace.

[![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_1_.jpg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%20401%20973%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_1_.jpg)

Membership

###  Montana Council - Customer-Facing Website

Many times, websites are built for existing customers, not potential
customers. The Montana Council made the strategic decision to tailor their web
content specifically for **__new__** customers.  In addition, they created
district pages that could be managed locally. Not only is the Montana Council
website streamlined and easy to navigate, it has robust analytics tools to
help staff and volunteers better understand what content is being utilized and
what customers need.

content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_2_-scaled-e1663005956128.jpg)

Membership

###  Greater St. Louis Area Council - Scouts, Today and Tomorrow

The extensive research and robust multi-channel marketing mix are two of the
standout components of this membership campaign.  With messaging that focused
less on __HOW__ to join…but instead more on __WHY__ to join…this campaign hit
all the right notes!

content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_3_-e1663006006111.jpg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%20900%20464%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_3_-e1663006006111.jpg)

Program Delivery

###  Blue Ridge Council - This Is Home

Musty tents?  Homesick kids?  Not a chance!  This camp promotional campaign
uses compelling video to drive demand and build the promise of Scouting’s
outdoor experiences.  It took basic Scouting activities and made them look
AMAZING!  The use of quick cuts, energetic music, and consistent thematic
elements tied it all together in a video execution that delivers!

[![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_4_-e1663006056651.jpg)![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%20900%20582%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_4_-e1663006056651.jpg)

Social / Digital Outreach

###  Atlanta Area Council - Campfire Stories

Great local stories…told on multiple channels…sourced from a team.  The use of
multiple content creators (a.k.a. District Professionals from across the
council) make this effort notable.  No need to rely on one particular person
with the task of mining good content when a lighter load can be spread across
a larger team.  Use all of the resources at your disposal to come up with
great content, and then utilize that content across multiple channels to
maximize your audience reach.  Add in a great hook like “Campfire Stories” and
you have an award-winning combination.  Well done Atlanta Area Council!

content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_5_-e1663005536369.jpg)](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/2022/09/featured-_5_-e1663005536369.jpg)

###  Piedmont Council - Annual Report

Most annual reports are sent to potential funders, presented to boards, and
included as part of grant proposals. This report was distributed through local
news media in an effort to communicate the impact of Scouting in the
community. In addition, the report has a very simple and clean design that is
consistent with the Piedmont Council’s website.

## JUDGING AND CRITERIA

![marketing awards line separator](https://www.scouting.org/wp-
content/uploads/elementor/thumbs/marketing-awards-line-separator-
qjjk7uuj82rfmti66hkoirvm0oek2nw8cl88rkjp7i.png)![marketing awards line
separator](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns=%22http://www.w3.org/2000/svg%22%20viewBox=%220%200%20210%20140%22%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Entries were accepted during the window of October 1, 2021 through February 15
2022 for pieces that were in-market during calendar year 2021. Entries were
submitted electronically and were broken out by category (Fundraising,
Membership, Program Implementation, Social/Digital Outreach) and by council
size within each category (100-200 size councils, 300-400 size councils, and
500+ size councils). Similarly-sized councils were judged with their peers.

Each entry was judged by three separate judges. The scores were added together
and the top three scoring entries in each category, for each council class
size, were awarded a 2022 National Marketing Award. In addition, seven
honorees were of particular note and were awarded the “Judges’ Choice”
designation.

The scoring rubric consisted of a 25 point scale based on:

## ADVANCED PLANNING

Up to 5 points – Assessment of research, needs identification, timetable,
goals, measurement strategies, etc.

### EXECUTION

Up to 5 points – What were the resources required? Were changes to the plan
required while executing the campaign? Were adaptations identified that would
improve the implementation next time or in another council?

### IMPACT

Up to 5 points – Did the project have the desired or projected impact? How
significant was the end result? Did it achieve a significant impact? In what
ways?

## CREATIVITY/ REPLICABILITY

Up to 5 points – Consideration will be given to pieces that are unique. The
ability to scale the concept to adapt to differing council sizes is a plus.

### LOOK & FEEL

Up to 5 points – Does the piece or campaign effectively represent the Scouting
brand or visually tell the Scouting story? Does the campaign or piece follow
BSA’s brand standards?

Note: No entries were received in the Social/Digital category for the 500+
council size.
